title: Explain behavior with telemetry
purpose: When a trade seems to disappear, a healthy service status gives little help. This chapter is for developers diagnosing a distributed workflow: use complementary telemetry signals to narrow a question, and learn why missing telemetry cannot settle it.
entryAssumptions: NATS and PostgreSQL carry the workflow, but scattered logs make diagnosis difficult.
concepts: A metric summarizes measurements; a log records an event; a trace relates timed operations. Correlation is evidence of a path, not proof that every business effect committed.
runtimePrerequisites: Use the state quickstart for tool versions, generation, start and stop commands. Run one local state at a time because ports and generated output directories are shared.

transitions.carriesForward: Replace internal messaging with NATS while preserving the trade-to-position workflow.
transitions.motivation: NATS and PostgreSQL carry the workflow, but scattered logs make diagnosis difficult.
transitions.increment: Add LGTM telemetry to connect a user action with logs, metrics and traces.
transitions.evidence: The signals provide complementary evidence. Record which services are represented and which gaps remain instead of treating an empty panel as a successful run. Missing telemetry can reflect selection, sampling or collection problems. It is not evidence that no trade exists.

before: NATS and PostgreSQL carry the workflow, but scattered logs make diagnosis difficult.
after: Add LGTM telemetry to connect a user action with logs, metrics and traces.

objectives.outcome: Correlate one trade with available logs, metrics and traces, and identify gaps in the observed request path.
Explain the evidence boundary: Missing telemetry can reflect selection, sampling or collection problems. It is not evidence that no trade exists.

walkthrough.action: Start this state and open Grafana through /grafana/ as described in the quickstart. Submit one small trade and note its time and identifier. Find the relevant service logs and metrics, and inspect any available trace for that request.
walkthrough.expected: The signals provide complementary evidence. Record which services are represented and which gaps remain instead of treating an empty panel as a successful run.

walkthrough.action: Change the dashboard time range to exclude the request and compare it with a range that includes it. If a trace is absent, inspect instrumentation and collection health before concluding the request did not run.
walkthrough.expected: Missing telemetry can reflect selection, sampling or collection problems. It is not evidence that no trade exists.

assessments.question: Can you diagnose a missing trade from an empty dashboard alone?
assessments.guidance: No. Check time range and collection, then reconcile the persisted trade and processing evidence. Name the limits of the available signals.

limitations: Missing telemetry can reflect selection, sampling or collection problems. It is not evidence that no trade exists.
This is an educational local demonstration. Passing its checks does not establish production readiness, financial settlement, or correctness under every failure mode.
